2026-11-21.title: The Entry of Mary, Mother of God, into the Temple
readings: Whoever does the will of my Father
2026-11-21.alt: Feast of the Presentation (Entry) of the Mother of God in the Temple. The story of the child Mary brought to the Temple by Joachim and Anne comes from early Christian Tradition (the Protoevangelium of James), not from Scripture; the feast celebrates her total dedication to God.
2026-11-21.verse: For whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother and sister and mother.
theo: The Church celebrates today the tradition that Mary, as a little child, was brought by her parents Joachim and Anne to the Temple and given to God. The details come from Tradition, not from the Gospels, but the meaning is biblical: like Samuel, whom Hannah “lent to the LORD”, Mary belonged wholly to God from the beginning. The little girl in the Temple would one day become the Temple, carrying God's Son in her womb.

In the Gospel Jesus' mother and brothers stand outside wanting to speak with him. Pointing to his disciples he says: “Whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother and sister and mother.” This is not a rejection of Mary but her highest praise: no one did the Father's will more completely than she who said, “let it be with me according to your word.” Paul's words fit her perfectly: rejoice, do not worry, pray with thanksgiving, think on whatever is true, honourable, just, pure and lovely.
outline: What did your parents give to God when they baptised you?
Mary, like Samuel, belongs to the Lord.
The peace of God guards our hearts.
“Whoever does the will of my Father is my mother.”
live: Parents: consecrate your children to God through Mary today.
Replace one negative conversation with a good word.
2026-11-21.prayer: Holy Mary, Mother of God, given to the Lord from childhood, teach us to belong wholly to God, to do the Father's will, and to rejoice always in your Son. Amen.

quick: Mary belonged wholly to God from the beginning.
Doing the Father's will is her true greatness.
2026-11-21.action: Consecrate your family to God through Mary today.
2026-11-21.question: What part of me have I not yet given to God?

homily: Dear friends, today the Church celebrates the tradition that Mary, Mother of God, as a little child was brought by her parents Joachim and Anne to the Temple and given to God. The details come from Tradition, not from the Gospels, but their meaning is clear: from the very beginning Mary's whole life was given to God, like Samuel whom Hannah lent to the Lord.

In the Gospel, when Jesus' mother and brothers stand outside, he points to his disciples and says: here are my mother and my brothers! Whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother and sister and mother (Matthew 12:49–50). Mary is Jesus' mother first not in the body but in a heart that received God's will.

Paul says: rejoice in the Lord always; whatever is true, honourable, just and pure, think about these things (Philippians 4:4, 8). This was Mary's heart. Today let us give our day to God with Mary; pray three Hail Marys and place this day in her hands. Amen.
kids: Children, little Mary was given to God. Today you too can say: God, this day is yours!

intro: Theme: “Whoever does the will of my Father.”

sub: Mary was wholly given to God and said yes.
q: For this child I prayed; and the LORD has granted me the petition that I made to him. Therefore I have lent him to the LORD; as long as he lives, he is given to the LORD.
Then Mary said, “Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word.”
points.apply: Consecrate your family to God through Mary.

sub: The psalmist carries God's law in his heart.
Jesus calls those who do the Father's will his mother.
q: I delight to do your will, O my God; your law is within my heart.
For whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother and sister and mother.
points.apply: Ask in prayer: Father, what is your will for me today?

sub: Paul: rejoice in the Lord always.
q: Sing aloud, O daughter Zion; shout, O Israel! Rejoice and exult with all your heart, O daughter Jerusalem!
Rejoice in the Lord always; again I will say, Rejoice.
points.apply: Replace one complaint with thanksgiving today.

concl: With her we do the Father's will and rejoice.
2026-11-21.resolve: Pray the Hail Mary for your family each evening.
